title: Do not let a test disable itself; exclude it at the runner level instead

facts.note: Any test case in any test file; the obligation is stack-neutral and not limited by language, test framework or whether the file is being changed. Bun-specific detection is implementation scope (see verifier_detail).
AST-level detection of skip/todo-style modifiers on test cases and of an env-guarded early return inside a test body; currently realized for bun:test by bun_tester_discipline_detector.

fires: A live smoke test begins with `if (!process.env.DATABASE_URL) return;` so it silently passes when the variable is absent.
An existing, unchanged test file already contains a self-skip or guarded bail.
doesNotFire: A `.skip`-like call or early return inside a fixture or helper that is not itself a test case.
A test excluded from a run via the runner's configuration filter.

given: A test case (it / test / describe) exists in a test suite
when: the test is disabled from inside its own source — a `.skip` / `.todo` / `.failing` modifier or an early `return` guarded on an environment check
then: Remove the self-disabling so the test actually runs (or delete the test); if it must not run somewhere, exclude it in the runner's configuration instead.
prefer: Remove the modifier and let the test run, or delete the test.
Exclude via a runner config filter: visible in configuration, not invisible in a green suite.
avoid: `if (!process.env.X) return` in a test body: same fault in disguise, more common, silent exactly where nobody watches.
`.failing` as a disabler. Source conflict: statement forbids it; self_skip term exempts `.fails`/`.failing` as core RED markers. Escalate, don't decide.
unless: Skip in a fixture/helper that is not itself a test case.
Runner-level exclusion (config filter), the supported way not to run a test.
why: A skipped test reports GREEN: the suite passes, the gate sees no failure, and the acceptance is recorded as covered by a test that did not run.
evidence: The detector reports no self_skip or guarded_bail finding for the test files in scope.
Any environment-specific non-execution is expressed as a runner configuration filter visible in config, not inside the test body.
verifier_detail: self_skip (term definition): `.skip` or `.todo` on it / test / describe (it.skip, test.skip, describe.skip, *.todo).

`.failing` — UNRESOLVED source conflict, both claims preserved: (a) statement: a test MUST NOT disable itself with `.skip` / `.todo` / `.failing`; summary: flags it.skip/test.skip/describe.skip (and `.todo` / `.failing`). (b) term self_skip: deliberately excludes `.fails` / `.failing`, which core's RED vocabulary lists as accepted markers. This rewrite does not choose; the verifier must surface `.failing` cases for authoritative resolution rather than silently pass or fail them.
guarded_bail: a guarded `if (…process.env…) return` bail-out inside a test (e.g. `if (!process.env.DATABASE_URL) return;` at the top of a live smoke).
Scope: only test cases; skips inside fixtures/helpers that are not themselves test cases are out of scope. Runner-level config exclusions (config filter) are not findings.

Stack-neutral obligation; the current detector is Bun-specific over `bun:test` modifiers, realized by bun_tester_discipline_detector (implementation type: validator). Bun scope and any changed-file filtering are implementation scope of the detector, not limits on the obligation.
Reason for runner-level exclusion: if a test genuinely cannot run somewhere, that belongs in the runner's configuration where it is visible, not hidden inside the test body.
